arxiv-2007-03492.title: Computing a maximum clique in geometric superclasses of disk graphs
arxiv-2007-03492.creator: Nicolas Grelier
arxiv-2007-03492.description: Abstract In the 90’s Clark, Colbourn and Johnson wrote a seminal paper where they proved that maximum clique can be solved in polynomial time in unit disk graphs. Since then, the complexity of maximum clique in intersection graphs of d d -dimensional (unit) balls has been investigated. For ball graphs, the problem is NP-hard, as shown by Bonamy et al.

arxiv-2205-00097.title: Fast and Scalable Human Pose Estimation using mmWave Point Cloud Conference: Proceedings of the 59th ACM/IEEE Design Automation Conference (DAC); July 10–14, 2022; San Francisco, CA, USA Price: 15.00 DOI: 10.1145/3489517.3530522 ISBN: 978-1-4503-9142-9/22/07
arxiv-2205-00097.creator: Sizhe An, Umit Y. Ogras
arxiv-2205-00097.description: Abstract . Millimeter-Wave (mmWave) radar can enable high-resolution human pose estimation with low cost and computational requirements. However, mmWave data point cloud, the primary input to processing algorithms, is highly sparse and carries significantly less information than other alternatives such as video frames.

arxiv-2211-16822.title: A Probabilistic-Logic based Commonsense Representation Framework for Modelling Inferences with Multiple Antecedents and Varying Likelihoods
arxiv-2211-16822.creator: Shantanu Jaiswal, Liu Yan, Dongkyu Choi, Kenneth Kwok
arxiv-2211-16822.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Shantanu Jaiswal, Liu Yan, Dongkyu Choi, Kenneth Kwok. Commonsense knowledge-graphs (CKGs) are important resources towards building machines that can ‘reason’ on text or environmental inputs and make inferences beyond perception. While current CKGs encode world knowledge for a large number of concepts and have been effectively utilized for incorporating commonsense in neural models, they primarily encode declarative or single-condition inferential knowledge and assume all conceptual beliefs to have the same likelihood.

arxiv-2310-10622.creator: W. A. van Wijngaarden, W. Happer
arxiv-2310-10622.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by W. A. van Wijngaarden, W. Happer. For 2 ​ n 2n -stream radiation transfer theory, a stack of m = 2 , 3 , 4 , … m=2,3,4,\ldots clouds can be represented as an equivalent cloud.

arxiv-2406-11533.title: High-Dimensional Subspace Expansion Using Classical Shadows
arxiv-2406-11533.creator: Gregory Boyd, Bálint Koczor, Zhenyu Cai
arxiv-2406-11533.description: Abstract We introduce a post-processing technique for classical shadow measurement data that enhances the precision of ground state estimation through high-dimensional subspace expansion; the dimensionality is only limited by the amount of classical post-processing resources rather than by quantum resources.

arxiv-2409-06783.title: Supermassive black hole feedback quenches disc galaxies and suppresses bar formation in TNG50
arxiv-2409-06783.creator: Matthew Frosst, Danail Obreschkow, Aaron Ludlow, Connor Bottrell, Shy Genel
arxiv-2409-06783.description: Abstract We use the cosmological magneto-hydrodynamical simulation TNG50 to study the relationship between black hole feedback, the presence of stellar bars, and star formation quenching in Milky Way-like disc galaxies. Of our sample of 198 discs, about 63 63 per cent develop stellar bars that last until z = 0 z=0 .

arxiv-2409-07335.title: Explanation, Debate, Align: A Weak-to-Strong Framework for Language Model Generalization
arxiv-2409-07335.creator: Mehrdad Zakershahrak, Samira Ghodratnama
arxiv-2409-07335.description: Abstract The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence systems has brought the challenge of AI alignment to the forefront of research, particularly in complex decision-making and task execution. As these systems surpass human-level performance in sophisticated problems, ensuring their alignment with human values, intentions, and ethical guidelines becomes crucial.

arxiv-2502-15815.title: Theoretical Physics Benchmark (TPBench) - a Dataset and Study of AI Reasoning Capabilities in Theoretical Physics
arxiv-2502-15815.creator: Daniel J.H. Chung, Zhiqi Gao, Yurii Kvasiuk, Tianyi Li, Moritz Münchmeyer, Maja Rudolph, Frederic Sala, Sai Chaitanya Tadepalli
arxiv-2502-15815.description: Abstract We introduce a benchmark to evaluate the capability of AI to solve problems in theoretical physics, focusing on high-energy theory and cosmology. The first iteration of our benchmark consists of 57 problems of varying difficulty, from undergraduate to research level. These problems are novel in the sense that they do not come from public problem collections.

arxiv-2505-14158.title: Temporal Alignment of Time Sensitive Facts with Activation Engineering
arxiv-2505-14158.creator: Sanjay Govindan, Maurice Pagnucco, Yang Song
arxiv-2505-14158.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) are trained on diverse and often conflicting knowledge spanning multiple domains and time periods. Some of this knowledge is only valid within specific temporal contexts, such as answering the question, “Who is the President of the United States in 2022?” Ensuring LLMs generate time appropriate responses is crucial for maintaining relevance and accuracy.

arxiv-2505-20777.title: TACO: Think-Answer Consistency for Optimized Long-Chain Reasoning and Efficient Data Learning via Reinforcement Learning in LVLMs
arxiv-2505-20777.creator: Zhehan Kan, Xinghua Jiang, Xin Li, Haoyu Cao, Yinsong Liu Deqiang Jiang Xing Sun Qingmin Liao Wenming Yang
arxiv-2505-20777.description: Abstract DeepSeek R1 has significantly advanced complex reasoning for large language models (LLMs). While recent methods have attempted to replicate R1’s reasoning capabilities in multimodal settings, they face limitations, including inconsistencies between reasoning and final answers, model instability and crashes during long-chain exploration, and low data learning efficiency.

pmc-10518751.title: Eruptive lentiginosis in resolving plaque psoriasis during treatment with risankizumab
pmc-10518751.creator: Gerardo Palmisano, Alessandro Di Stefani, Simone Cappilli, Andrea Chiricozzi, Ketty Peris
pmc-10518751.description: zumab. A 30‐year‐old woman was examined for a 10‐year history of severe chronic psoriasis vulgaris. Previous treatments included cyclosporin and adalimumab, and were ineffective. Physical examination showed generalized, thick, dry, scaly plaques on the back, upper and lower limbs, involving more than 50% of body surface area (PASI 10).

pmc-11355759.title: Performance of a Ship-Based Cupronickel Alloy in Exposure Conditions of Arabian Seawater—A Comparative Study
pmc-11355759.creator: Syed Ali Sarfraz, Muntazir Abbas, Nasir Mahmood Ahmad
pmc-11355759.description: Cupronickel-based alloys are widely known for their excellent resistance against aqueous corrosion, however, they can be susceptible to corrosion at accelerated rates and premature failure when exposed to a polluted or brackish seawater medium, even for short-term exposure durations. This unfamiliar corrosion behavior may be a result of the formation of an unprotected corrosion film during the early exposure durations.

pmc-12541971.title: Activating NEDD4L suppresses EGFR-driven lung adenocarcinoma growth via facilitating EGFR proteasomal degradation
pmc-12541971.creator: Maojian Chen, Wei Jiang, Jianhua Zhan, Shaoping Zhang, Jiani Zheng, Yihua Huang, Junyi He, Yunpeng Yang, Shen Zhao, Yaxiong Zhang, Jiaqing Liu, Lanlan Pang, Li Zhang, Wenfeng Fang, Jing Li
pmc-12541971.description: BackgroundResistant mutations and amplification of the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), followed by the upregulation of its translated protein undermines the efficacy of EGFR-tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) in EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). This underscores that promoting EGFR protein degradation may be a promising strategy for treatment.

pmc-12656134.title: Characterization of Hottentotta judaicus Scorpion Venom: Toxic Effects and Neurobehavioral Modulation in Insect Models
pmc-12656134.creator: Rim Wehbe, Aline Karaki, Zeina Dassouki, Mohamad Rima, Adolfo Borges, Rabih Roufayel, Christian Legros, Ziad Fajloun, Zakaria Kambris
pmc-12656134.description: Scorpion venom is a rich source of diverse bioactive molecules with medicinal importance. While the venoms of many Buthidae scorpions have been extensively studied for their toxicity and therapeutic potential, Hottentotta judaicus scorpion venom (HjSV) remains poorly explored. In this study, using LC-ESI-MS, we show that HjSV has a complex composition.

pmc-12733309.title: A Composite Score of Insulin Resistance and Inflammation Biomarkers for Predicting Lower Limb Complications in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
pmc-12733309.creator: Adina Mitrea, Adela-Gabriela Ștefan, Ionela-Mihaela Vladu, Diana Clenciu, Sorina-Ionelia Stan, Ion-Cristian Efrem, Viorel Biciușcă, Moța Maria, Diana-Cristina Protasiewicz-Timofticiuc, Maria-Magdalena Roșu, Theodora-Claudia Radu-Gheonea, Eugen Moța, Gabriel Mogoș, Delia-Viola Reurean-Pintilei, Lidia
pmc-12733309.description: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is a chronic non-communicable disease associated with macroangiopathy and microangiopathy, with disabling or even life-threatening complications. In the present study, we aimed to analyze the association between insulin resistance (IR) and inflammation biomarkers and peripheral arterial disease (PAD) and diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN), respectively.

pmc-12835016.title: Multi-factor authentication and key agreement scheme based on PUF and Chebyshev chaotic map for wireless sensor networks
pmc-12835016.creator: Linjie Wang, Chunxia Han
pmc-12835016.description: Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) communication systems represent a flexible, reliable, and efficient paradigm that enables bidirectional real-time data exchange, as well as mutual identity authentication between the User and the Sensor Node. However, due to the open nature of these networks, communications among entities may be intercepted or manipulated by attackers through public channels at any time.

pmc-13159232.title: Impact of interventions addressing perinatal mental health on loneliness and/or satisfaction with social support: systematic review
pmc-13159232.creator: Cristina Vasquez, Apphia Ruth D’souza, Rebecca Nowland, Billie Lever Taylor, Katherine Adlington, Eiluned Pearce, Alexandra Pitman
pmc-13159232.description: ObjectivesLoneliness and low social support are associated with poor mental health in the perinatal period (pregnancy and one year postnatal). However, no reviews have explored systematically whether interventions aimed at improving perinatal mental health also improve loneliness and/or social support satisfaction (SSS).

pmc-13377700.title: Rational structural design for the dual enhancement of catalytic activity and thermal stability of hyaluronidase from Citrobacter portucalensis
pmc-13377700.creator: Yuanying Zhu, Shijunyin Chen, Feiyang Li, Yaya Yao, Yuejia Ji, Wei Feng, Zhongkai Wang, Xuepeng Li, Haitao Yue
pmc-13377700.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Hyaluronidases (HAase) offer a practical route to produce valued low molecular weight hyaluronic acid (LMW-HA) and HA oligosaccharides (o-HA), which are valued across medical, cosmetic, and biomaterials applications due to their enhanced bioactivity and tissue penetration. However, reliable production and scale-up of LMW‑HA and o‑HA remain complicated due to inefficient production method, potential pathogenic hosts, enzymes with limited catalytic proficiency and prone to thermal denaturation.

pmc-13415903.title: A systematic review of the pharmacokinetics of classical serotonergic psychedelic compounds in healthy adult subjects
pmc-13415903.creator: Elliot Hampsey, Kirsty Martin, Michail Kalfas, Louis Benson, Sirid Wihlborg, Luke Jelen, Allan H. Young, James Rucker
pmc-13415903.description: Introduction:Despite renewed investigations into classical psychedelic compounds, their pharmacokinetic profiles remain incompletely understood.Methods:This systematic review collated data from healthy adult volunteers on the pharmacokinetic properties of lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD), psilocybin, dimethyltryptamine (DMT), mescaline, and 5-methoxy-N,N-dimethyltryptamine (5-MEO-DMT).Results:We identified 32 eligible trials. LSD was the most studied compound, followed by DMT, split between intravenous (IV) and oral formulations.
